findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

The nozzle on the fountain drink machine in the Mellow Yellow spot was observed with a heavy build up of soilage. The PIC was shown and cleaned the item, as well as the rest of the nozzles to correct the immediate violation. Ensure that the food contact surfaces are cleaned often enough to prevent accumulation of filth.

findings.title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
findings.citation_text:
4-302.12 Food Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. (B) A TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE with a suitable small-diameter probe that is designed to measure the temperature of thin masses shall be provided and readily accessible to accurately measure the temperature in thin FOODS such as MEAT patties and FISH filets.

The PIC was unable to find a probe style thermometer at the time of the inspection. The inspector will follow-up in 10 days to ensure that a probe thermometer is acquired and available at the facility.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.111(C) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (C) Using methods, if pests are found, such as trapping devices or other means of pest control as specified under §§ 7-202.12, 7-206.12, and 7-206.13.

Over a dozen gnats were observed in the dish area of the facility. The PIC was shown and instructed to remove prior to the next routine inspection. They stated that they were only there because the fryers were cleaned. The inspector stated that the flys should still be removed and prevented from returning. While the inspector was typing the report the PIC stated that the situation was fixed. They sprayed the sanitizer used by the facility throughout the area, killing the flys that were observable. The inspector is willing to accept the situation is currently managed with the caveat that a spot check will be conducted in the next week or so to verify that the flys do not return.

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. 

At the time of the inspection there was not a person with the requisite allergen training certificate available in the facility. The situation was discussed with the PIC and they are instructed to have someone with the requisite training available in the facility at all times that it is in operation.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

At the time of the inspection there was not a CFPM available at the facility. The PIC is instructed to maintain enough CFPMs on staff to cover all shifts in the facility moving forward.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12(A) Cleaning Procedure. (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands or arms for at least 20 seconds, using a cleaning compound in a HANDWASHING SINK that is equipped as specified under § 5-202.12 and Subpart 6-301. 

An employee was observed to rinse their hands quickly in the hand sink without taking the requisite time or using soap. Education was conducted and will be followed-up on with the use of a translator in the future.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD.

A food handler was observed to change gloves without hand washing. Education was conducted and will be followed-up on at the educational visit in the future.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

An employee was observed to wash hands and use their bare hands to turn off the faucet with their bare hands. Education was conducted and will be followed-up on at the future educational visit.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.citation_text:
6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

The hand sink in the bathroom was without hand soap at the time of the inspection. The PIC was instructed to replace the soap and a cup of soap was provided to correct the immediate violation. Ensure that all hand sinks are properly supplied at all times.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11(A) Equipment Food-Contact Surfaces and Utensils. (A) Equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be cleaned: (5) At any time during the operation when contamination may have occurred.

Several items were observed stored on the shelving after being cleaned and with remaining food debris on them. The PIC was shown and instructed to have the items cleaned again. The dishes were re-cleaned to correct. Ensure that all dishes are completely cleaned prior to storage and future use in the faiclity.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used.
findings.comment:
3-501.13(A-E) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed in an approved manner. 

Raw fish are observed stored in the three part sink thawing in standing water. Education was conducted and the fish moved to a bucket to allow for running water. This is an ongoing issue at this facility. Ensure that all TCS foods are thawed in an approved manner at all times.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.citation_text:
3-307.11 Miscellaneous Sources of Contamination. FOOD shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301 - 3-306. 

An open can of strawberry glaze was observed in the walk in cooler without effective covering. The PIC was shown and instructed to ensure that all containers of food are protected from possible contamination at all times that they are not actively in use.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

The roof of the microwave was observed heavily soiled with food splash. One of the food handlers in the kitchen wiped the microwave out with a sani rag to correct. Ensure that the non-food contact surfaces are cleaned regularly to prevent possible incidental contamination of foods place inside.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
findings.citation_text:
6-403.11(A) Designated Areas. (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use TOBACCO PRODUCTS shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination.

Multiple employee drinks (some partially consumed) were observed in the walk in cooler on shelving and intermixed (next to and above) foods intended for consumers. Education was conducted with the PIC. The items should be stored separately from foods intended for consumers moving forward.

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. 

At the time of the inspection there was not a person with the requisite allergen training certificate available in the facility. The situation was discussed with the PIC and they are instructed to have someone with the requisite training available in the facility at all times that it is in operation.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used.
findings.comment:
3-501.13(A-E) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed in an approved manner. 

Raw fish are observed stored in the three part sink thawing in standing water. The PIC was shown and stated that a bucket was intended for this purpose to allow for running water. The fish was placed into the bucket during this inspection and begun to have running water during this inspection to correct. Ensure that all TCS foods are thawed in an approved manner at all times.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
findings.citation_text:
3-304.12(C) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (C) On a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food-contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized at a frequency specified under §§ 4-602.11 and 4-702.11.

A knife was observed stored in the small gap between shelving and wall in the northern most prep cooler. The PIC was shown and stated that it was there to help keep the lid open. The knife was removed and observed soled with food debris. It was moved to dish for cleaning to correct. Ensure that soiled utensils are stored so that they do not contaminate surfaces in the facility that are not easily cleanable. Ensure that items intended to not be food contact surfaces are not used as food contact surfaces.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.citation_text:
4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. 

The display cooler in the customer area of the facility is holding foods at 46F internal temperature. The only items in this cooler that are a Time/Temperature Control for Safety (TCS) food are individually packaged cheesecakes. Per the PIC these items were removed from the freezer in the back approximately three hours ago. The items were allowed to be placed back into the freezer for rapid re-cooling and retention. The PIC dissassembled the cooler’s cover and cleaned the vent during this inspection. The cooler reduced its temperature almost immediately and the violation is considered corrected at this time. Ensure that all coolers are operating correctly at all times.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.citation_text:
3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

1) A package of onions is observed on the floor in the back corner of the walk in cooler. 2) A stack of boxes of food are observed in the back corner of the walk in freezer with the bottom box directly on the floor. The PIC was notified and instructed to store all foods off of the ground at all times, including in the walk in cooler/freezer. Ensure that all food items are stored off of the floor at all times in the facility. A similar situation was observed and noted on the previous routine inspection.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-101.11(A)(3) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (3) Nonabsorbent for areas subject to moisture such as FOOD preparation areas, walk-in refrigerators, WAREWASHING areas, toilet rooms, mobile FOOD ESTABLISHMENT SERVICING AREAS, and areas subject to flushing or spray cleaning methods.

There is a gap observed between the sink and the wall in the bathroom. The PIC was notified and instructed to re-seal the location so that it is smooth and easily cleanable prior to the next routine inspection. Ensure that all surfaces subject to moisture and/or foods are sealed so that they are smooth and easily cleanable.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.citation_text:
2-301.11 Clean Condition. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall keep their hands and exposed portions of their arms clean.

Employees were observed to wash hands and turn off the faucet with their bare hands, thus recontaminating their hands prior to food handling. The PIC was consulted and instructed to review hand washing moving forward. Use a clean barrier to turn off the hand sink so as not to re-contaminate your hands prior to food service. Education conducted to correct.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Multiple nozzles on the fountain drink machine are observed soiled inside of the nozzles with pink, black, green or yellow slime/mold. The items were shown to the PIC and moved to dish for cleaning. He stated that the nozzles are cleaned weekly. This is not sufficient. The nozzles should be cleaned every few days at most to prevent the inevitable accumulation that they develop. Ensure that they are cleaned often enough to prevent build ups of potentially pathogenic organisms.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
findings.citation_text:
7-102.11 Common Name. Working containers used for storing POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS such as cleaners and SANITIZERS taken from bulk supplies shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material.

On arrival and during the inspection the spray bottle used for the sanitizer in the service area is without a label. A label was added during this inspection to correct. Ensure that all chemicals not in their original containers have labeling indicating the common name of the chemical in them at all times that they are in use.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used.
findings.comment:
3-501.13(A-E) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed in an approved manner. 

Raw fish are observed stored in the three part sink thawing in standing water. This was noticed while the inspector was washing their hands ant the beginning of the inspection and the PIC began running water before the situation could be addressed directly. Ensure that all TCS foods are thawed in an approved manner at all times.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.citation_text:
3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

A box of frozen meat is observed on the floor under a table in the kitchen during this inspection. The PIC was shown and moved the box to a shelf in the walk in cooler to correct. Ensure that all foods are stored so that they are at least six inches above the floor at all times.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. 

Cheesecake in the display cooler located in the consumer area is observed with an internal temperature of 48F. Temperatures throughout the cooler are observed acceptable (39F-41F) in the top section of the cooler and become progressively warmer as you move down the cooler. Cheesecake and pudding cups are the only items in this cooler needing temperature control for safety. As the PIC was consulted the retractable cover was pulled down to help contain the cool air produced by the unit. Per the PIC the cheesecake and pudding were placed in the unit after lunch (.5-1 hour prior to inspection). They were moved to the walk in to save while the cooler was given time to cool down. This does not seem to be effective during his inspection. The TCS items will be stored in the top of the cooler moving forward and maintenance is to be called to check the cooler over. It is also suggested to use extra thermometers (one is in the unit and is accurate) in this unit to see what temperatures different locations in the unit register at. Inspector will spot check after the fair to ensure that the cooler is functioning or that the new storage practice is being maintained.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
3-307.11: FOOD shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301-3-306. 

A used cigar is observed behind the lid in the prep cooler next to the kitchen door. It is saturated with condensation. The PIC was shown and the cigar removed to correct the immediate violation. Smoking should not be taking place in the kitchen at any time to prevent contamination of food contact surfaces of foods.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. 

The wall/floor junction under and behind the prep cooler and counters is heavily in need of cleaning. The PIC was notified and instructed to clean and maintain clean moving forward. Per the PIC the equipment is supposed to be moved away from the wall and cleaned twice a week. This does not appear to be happening at this time. Re-training and education are suggested, but the facility must stay clean.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions. 

Approximately 10 small live ants are observed around the drain in the bathroom. The PIC was shown the location and instructed to contact their pest control agency (Nelson’s Termite and Pest) for remediation. Follow up to be conducted in two weeks for compliance.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
(REPEAT x2) 2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.

An employee was observed to change gloves without washing hands. This took place while moving from raw TCS foods to Ready-To-Eat TCS foods. A conversation took place with the PIC and education conducted. Ensure hand washing takes place at all applicable times!

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. 

The hand sink in the bathroom is pulling away from the wall, producing a gap/crack that is not easily cleanable. The PIC is instructed to reseal the gap. He stated that caulk was available and that it would be re-caulked in the near future.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
6-403.11: (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use tobacco shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be located in a designated room or area where contamination of FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES cannot occur. 

Employee foods/drinks are observed on a shelf mixed in with and over foods intended for consumers. The PIC was consulted and a location should be designated for employee foods and protect from possible contamination of consumer foods.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.  

An employee was observed to change gloves multiple times throughout the inspection without washing their hands. Hand washing was discussed and the PIC should ensure that effective hand washing takes place at each time that it is required. Wash hands between glove changes.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED. 

An employee was observed to wash their hands and then use their bare hands to turn off the faucet. Education was conducted and the PIC is instructed to ensure that proper hand washing is taking place in the facility.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria.

On arrival the remaining spray bottles of sanitizer in the facility are observed low. The PIC indicated that this afternoon’s truck has their next batch of sanitizer. To provide sanitizer until then a bottle of bleach was acquired and a solution made during this inspection to correct. Ensure that sanitizers are available and of sufficient concentration at all times of operation.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.comment:
3-501.13: TCS FOOD shall be thawed: (A) at 41F or below in refrigeration (B) completely submerged under RUNNING water, not getting above 41F (water temp of 70F or below). If food will be cooked, not getting above 41F for more than 4 hours. (C) part of the cooking process (D) Using any procedure if RTE FOOD is thawed and prepared for immediate service (E) ROP FISH that bear label shall be removed from packaging before thawing under refrigeration, upon completion of thawing from running water. 

Beef and shrimp are observed thawing in standing water in the separate sections of the three part sink. This is a poor practice and needs to stop. Running water is needed for this type of thawing. The PIC was instructed to use the available tubs in the dish room as an option that allows for flowing water in the thawing process. Running water was provided during this inspection to correct the violation.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
6-501.110: (A) Dressing rooms shall be used by EMPLOYEES if the EMPLOYEES regularly change their clothes in the establishment. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be used for the orderly storage of EMPLOYEE clothing and other possessions. 

1) A jacket is observed stored alongside of clean dishes in the dish room. 2) A purse and scarf are observed stored next to clean dishes in the dish room. PIC was consulted and the items moved to the back room where they should be stored (per the PIC) to correct.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  

Food handler cards are not available for the food handlers at the facility during this inspection. PIC is instructed to ensure that all food handlers have an ANSI accredited food handler certification available during the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
2-103.11: (O) FOOD EMPLOYEES are informed in verifiable manner of their responsibility to report accordance with LAW, to PIC, information about their health related to disease transmissible through FOOD.  

Reporting agreements are not available for employees at this facility during this inspection. A fresh copy of the SCDPH Reporting Agreement was given to the PIC during this inspection. They stated that the other owner/manager had the paperwork and would send copies to the inspector’s email. Ensure that copies are sent prior to the follow up dates. Due to the fair taking place on the usual follow up date, The follow up will be pushed back to 8/22/23.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.  

A food employee was observed to don gloves without hand washing. Education conducted. PIC is instructed to review when hand washing is applicable and ensure that food handlers wash hands when needed.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.  

A food handler was observed to move from handling raw chicken to handling raw fish without changing gloves/ hand washing. Education conducted. PIC is to review with employees when to wash hands and ensure that hand washing is taking place when it should.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. 

The hand sink in the kitchen area is blocked with a stack of boxes as well as a wheeled trolly. PIC was consulted and the items removed so that the sink is easily accessible. Ensure that the hand sinks are maintained easily accessible at all times to promote consistent hand washing.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Multiple items in the “clean” section of the dish room are observed with food debris still soiling them. PIC was consulted and the items moved back to dish to correct. Ensure that the dish washers always clean the food contact items thoroughly prior to storage and subsequent use.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
7-201.11: (A)-(B) POISONOUS MATERIALS shall be stored to prevent contamination of FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES by separating or locating MATERIALS in area away or below FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES (use partition or store below). 

A can of RAID is observed stored on a shelf both behind cleaned food contact surfaces as well as over food contact surfaces. PIC was consulted. The RAID was moved to the bottom shelf where other chemicals are to be stored.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
7-301.11: (B) POISONOUS MATERIALS shall be located in area not above FOOD or FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES. 

Containers of chemicals (cleaners, sanitizers and degreasers) are stored on shelves above food contact surfaces in the dish area. Education conducted and the items moved to the bottom shelf during this inspection to correct.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
3-307.11: FOOD shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301-3-306. 

The ambient air thermometer in the raw meat prep cooler is observed laying in the tub of raw fish. PIC was consulted and the thermometer moved to correct the violation. Ensure that the equipment not often cleaned/sanitized is maintained out of the foods to protect them from contamination.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
3-304.14: (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. 

A moist cloth in the kitchen is observed stored on the counter. PIC consulted and instructed to either use paper towels in conjunction with the available spray bottles or use buckets of sanitizer in conjunction with the available cloths so that they can be stored between uses in solution. PIC indicate that paper towels will be used moving forward.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
6-403.11: (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use tobacco shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be located in a designated room or area where contamination of FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES cannot occur. 

1) Cups with drink in them are observed in the dry storage area and the dish area. Items are without lids/straws. PIC consulted and the cups removed to correct the violation. Ensure that employee drinks are stored/ consumed in a way that does not pose a chance of contaminating foods or food contact surfaces. Lids and straws were discussed as well as a tub intended for employee foods. 2) An employee phone is observed on a charger sitting on top of aluminum tubs in the dish area. A discussion took place with the PIC and the phone moved so that it does not pose a risk of contaminating foods contact items. The tub noted was discarded. 3) Multiple cups appear to contain breakfast for employees and are stored over food contact items. Education discussed and the foods discarded. Stored employee foods so that they are not a concern for contaminating food contact surfaces.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  

Food handler cards are not available for the food handlers at the facility during this inspection. PIC is instructed to ensure that all food handlers have an ANSI accredited food handler certification available during the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

Allergen training certification is not available for the CFPM at the facility during this inspection. A hand out was given and they are instructed to have the certificate available at the next routine inspection.
